result.summary: The chapter turns to the house of Agenor. Europa is carried off by Zeus as a bull, her brothers scatter in search of her, and her sons by Zeus quarrel and part ways. Minos becomes king of Crete with Poseidon's bull, and Pasiphae's passion for it leads to the birth of the Minotaur.

scenes.title: Europa carried off; her kin scatter
scenes.summary: Agenor's family is traced, Zeus carries Europa to Crete as a bull, and her brothers, mother and Thasus search and then settle in various lands.
scenes.stakes: Agenor's family loses Europa and, bound by his order not to return without her, her kin are exiled.

scenes.title: Europa's sons quarrel over Miletus
scenes.summary: Asterius raises Europa's sons, who quarrel over Miletus. Minos wins, Miletus and Sarpedon found cities or kingdoms abroad, and Minos marries and has many children.
scenes.stakes: The brothers risk exile and defeat in their rivalry for a boy's affection.

scenes.title: Minos and the sea bull
scenes.summary: Minos claims the kingdom as the gods' gift and prays to Poseidon for a bull. He gets the throne but keeps the bull and sacrifices another.
scenes.stakes: Minos risks his claim to the throne and Poseidon's anger.

scenes.title: Pasiphae, Daedalus and the Minotaur
scenes.summary: Poseidon makes Pasiphae love the bull. Daedalus builds a wooden cow, and she bears the Minotaur, who is shut in the Labyrinth.
scenes.stakes: Pasiphae and Minos suffer Poseidon's vengeance, and Daedalus is already exiled for murder.

alias_notes.explanation: The Minotaur was named Asterius, like Europa's husband.

notable_quotes.reason: Defines the Labyrinth as a chamber of tangled windings.

analysis.text: Divine desire and broken promises drive the story: Zeus's passion and Minos's cheating of Poseidon bring exile and monstrous consequences.
The genealogies link Greek and Near Eastern peoples, deriving names like Cilicia, Thasus and Miletus from heroic founders.

legacy.text: The rape of Europa gave Europe its name in tradition and became a frequent subject in ancient and later European art.
The Minotaur and Labyrinth remain lasting symbols of maze and monster in literature and art.

fun_facts.text: The Library is attributed to Apollodorus, but is probably a work of the first or second century AD.

language_notes.text: The Heraclids are the descendants of Heracles, whose line the preceding chapters traced from Inachus through Belus and Danaus.
"Begat" is archaic for "fathered"; "aforesaid" refers to the sons already named, Aegyptus and Danaus.
Homer's Iliad makes Sarpedon a Lycian ally of Troy and a son of Zeus by Laodamia, contradicting the Europa tradition.
"Divers" means various or several; "took up their abode" means settled.
"Stipulated for a share" means he bargained, as the price of his help, to receive part of the land.
Rhadamanthys became a judge of the dead, a role Minos shares in later tradition for their just reputations.
"To wit" means "namely"; the sentence is a catalogue of Minos' children by different mothers.
Minos' control of the sea refers to his legendary fleet, often called a thalassocracy (sea empire).
The quoted line is a poetic description of the Labyrinth, quoted from an earlier poet; Theseus later kills the Minotaur there.

context_notes.text: Zeus often took animal shapes to approach mortal women; the bull abduction gave Europe its name in later tradition.
Minos uses a public prayer as a test of divine favor to win a disputed succession.
Daedalus was a legendary Athenian craftsman who fled to Crete after killing his nephew, according to tradition.
The Minotaur's name means "bull of Minos"; his given name Asterius repeats that of his stepfather.

literary_notes.text: The narrator offers an alternative parentage, typical of this book's habit of recording competing myths rather than choosing one.
Minos' keeping the bull sets up the divine punishment that follows.
Poseidon's revenge turns the bull Minos kept into the source of shame within Minos' own household.
The Minotaur's hybrid body, half bull and half human, embodies the unnatural union that produced him.
